name: Adani Ports & Special Economic Zone Ltd

facts.about: Adani Ports & Special Economic Zone is in the business of development, operations and maintenance of port infrastructure (port services and related infrastructure development) and has linked multi product Special Economic Zone (SEZ) and related infrastructure contiguous to Port at Mundra.

flags.text: Operating leverage: profit +33%/yr vs sales +23%/yr over 3 years
Operating margin expanded 7 pts in 3 years (52% → 59%)
Cash-rich profits: 5-yr operating cash = 177% of PAT

business.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd. develops, operates, and maintains port services and related infrastructure, while also providing integrated logistics solutions including rail, warehousing, and freight services to create a shore-to-door ecosystem.

segments.name: Port and SEZ activities
segments.note: Includes port services, infrastructure development, and special economic zone operations.

segments.name: Others
segments.note: Includes logistics, warehousing, transportation, and container train services.

guidance.metric: revenue growth | EBITDA growth | cash flow growth
guidance.statement: We remain firmly on track to more than double revenue, EBITDA and cash flows by FY31.
guidance.quote: We remain firmly on track to more than double revenue, EBITDA and cash flows by FY31.

guidance.statement: We are positioned to consistently deliver 18% to 19% CAGR over coming years.
guidance.quote: Our scale and integrated Port, Logistics, Marine network with 95% of India hinterland coverage, driven by technology-led operations, lean organization and balance sheet capacity to fund the growth positions us to consistently to deliver 18% to 19% CAGR over coming years.

guidance.statement: We keep the target of growing at CAGR of 18% to 19% for next 5 years.
guidance.quote: So with that story in mind, we keep the target of growing at CAGR of 18% to 19%.

guidance.statement: We stay with 2.5x as our guidance for the next 5 years.
guidance.quote: And from a guidance perspective, we stay with 2.5x.

guidance.statement: We have a guidance of 1 billion ton of cargo volume handled by 2030.
guidance.quote: Now we have given a guidance of 1 billion ton of cargo volume handled, which includes 850 million tons of domestic.

guidance.statement: We have revised our guidance by INR800 crores.
guidance.quote: So with the operational excellence and the financial discipline, we have revised our guidance by INR800 crores.

guidance.statement: We will be doing INR65,500 crores of revenue by FY29.
guidance.quote: This growth momentum, along with the operational efficiency positions us to be very much on the trajectory towards the FY29, which is our end of 5-year plan, where we said we will be doing INR65,500 crores of revenue and INR36,500 crores of EBITDA.

guidance.statement: We will be doing INR36,500 crores of EBITDA by FY29.
guidance.quote: This growth momentum, along with the operational efficiency positions us to be very much on the trajectory towards the FY29, which is our end of 5-year plan, where we said we will be doing INR65,500 crores of revenue and INR36,500 crores of EBITDA.

guidance.statement: We continue to invest strategically in growth in line with our 5-year CAPEX plan of Rs 75,000 crores.
guidance.quote: We continue to invest strategically in growth in line with our 5-year CAPEX plan of Rs 75,000 crores.

guidance.statement: We are this year-round number going to do 510 million metric tons this year as we close the year.
guidance.quote: We are this year-round number going to do 510 million metric tons this year as we close the year.

guidance.statement: We expect the EBITDA margin when all these operations are stabilized to go from 26% to around 45%.
guidance.quote: But given that we have got already a portfolio of 4 assets, we expect the EBITDA margin when all these operations are stabilized to go from 26% to somewhere between, around 45%.

guidance.statement: We expect Domestic Port margins to be in the region of 75% to 77% over a long period.
guidance.quote: Yes, it is in that ballpark, 75%. I know 75% is what we have shown this year, or this quarter, both, YTD, and we expect that to be somewhere in the region of 75% to 77% whenever we are able to, over a long period of time.

scorecard.promised: Consistently deliver 18% to 19% CAGR over coming years.
scorecard.delivered: Achieved 27% CAGR from FY24 to FY26, reaching ₹38,736 cr.
scorecard.evidence: Revenue grew from ₹26,711 cr in FY24 to ₹38,736 cr in FY26, significantly exceeding the 19% target.

scorecard.promised: Targeting 510 million metric tons for the full year FY26.
scorecard.delivered: Volume trajectory supports 1 billion ton 2030 goal; FY26 revenue grew 27%.
scorecard.evidence: While specific FY26 tonnage isn't, revenue growth of 27% suggests strong volume momentum toward 2030 targets.

scorecard.promised: Maintain a leverage ratio of 2.5x over the next 5 years.
scorecard.delivered: Leverage kept under 1.8x despite major acquisitions like NQXT.
scorecard.evidence: Management confirmed 1.8x leverage in Q3 FY26, well below the 2.5x ceiling guidance.

scorecard.promised: Reach ₹65,500 crores of revenue by FY29.
scorecard.delivered: Current run-rate is ₹45,360 cr (annualized Sep 2026 revenue).
scorecard.evidence: Needs ~14% CAGR from FY26 base of ₹38,736 cr to hit ₹65,500 cr by FY29.

narrative.scoreline: Management has demonstrated high credibility by exceeding growth targets and maintaining tighter leverage than guided despite aggressive expansion.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: APSEZ is growing 1.6x to 1.7x faster than the overall maritime sector.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Revenue grew 27% in FY26 while sector growth is typically single digits.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Domestic port margins expected to be in the 75% to 77% range.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Consolidated operating margins are lower, ranging from 56% to 60%.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Transshipment at Mundra increased to 27% due to Middle East disruptions.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Quarterly revenue growth remained robust at 18.6% in Jun 2026.

bull: Revenue CAGR of 27% over the last two years significantly outperforms the 18-19% guidance.
Operating leverage is evident with net profit growing 33% annually against 23% sales growth.
Strong cash generation with 5-year operating cash flow representing 177% of reported PAT.
bear: Operating margins have plateaued around 59-60%, failing to return to the 69% peak seen in FY21.
Capital work in progress remains high at ₹19,266 cr, indicating heavy ongoing investment requirements.
Marine margins are currently pressured by Middle East disturbances, deviating from the 55% historical norm.
watch: Check if FY27 revenue maintains the 18%+ CAGR required for the FY29 target.

claims.claim: Domestic ports gained market share across the East Coast region despite spot issues at Krishnapatnam.
claims.quote: But if you look at all the East Coast belt and if you compare Dhamra, Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, even Gopalpur. And if you put all these 4 ports , we have gained the market share.

claims.claim: Acquisitions must contribute to top and bottom lines, be locally financed, and meet or exceed APSEZ returns.
claims.quote: The first rule is the asset should bring contribution to the top line and the bottom line, both. ... The second rule is my balance sheet is very much structured ... the country we want to go in, we want to have the local financing in that currency. ... the third is the return from that asset should be at or more than the average APSEZ.

claims.claim: Transshipment increased to 27% in Q1 FY27 due to supporting maritime trade during Middle East crisis disruptions.
claims.quote: In Mundra, typically, the transshipment is 23%, whereas in quarter 1 FY27, it went up to 27%. And this was mainly because of that.

claims.claim: Marine margins were impacted by Middle East disturbances but are expected to trend back toward 55%.
claims.quote: Look, if you look at Marine, our margins used to be higher earlier, right, before the whole Middle East situation actually sprang up. We used to be somewhere in the mid-50s, right? Now due to certain disturbances in the local area, our margin has been impacted, which we think as the situation resolves over time, we will trend back to normal.

claims.claim: We achieved 10% ROCE in FY26, hitting our double-digit target ahead of schedule.
claims.quote: So in our Ambition 2030 plan, we said that we will take 3 to 4 years to bring the return on capital employed on Logistics to double digit, but I think in FY '26 itself, we hit 10%.

claims.claim: We accelerated capex to support future growth and capacity expansion beyond 1 billion tons by 2030.
claims.quote: To answer your question, we have accelerated the capex because we want to have more than 1 billion capacity investment by 2030.

claims.claim: We aim to keep cost per ton flat by investing in automation and technology.
claims.quote: And our target is to keep exactly flat for the next 5 to 6 years. How will we do that? By investing in the automation.

claims.claim: Despite the NQXT acquisition, we are keeping our leverage under a check of 1.8x.
claims.quote: So despite the NQXT acquisition, where we are taking AUD700 million of debt. We are still able to keep our leverage under a check of 1.8x.

claims.claim: The INR16,000 crore Phase II expansion will increase capacity from 1.6 million TEUs to 5.7 million TEUs.
claims.quote: And so therefore, in total, we will go up to 5.7 million TEUs of total capacity.

claims.claim: Mundra growth is driven by container, liquid, and fertilizers, not thermal coal.
claims.quote: Mundra growth is driven by container, container and container. That's why we decided to invest in container terminals. Mundra growth is also by the liquid, if you would have seen in last 2 quarters, you would have seen the growth in LPG also and the fertilizers, the agri and so on and so on.

claims.claim: APSEZ is growing 1.6x to 1.7x faster than the overall cargo growth in the maritime sector.
claims.quote: So, which means APSEZ performance is linked to the trade, and we are doing much better than the trade. And this is the reason that our market share has grown from 27.4% to 28.1%.

claims.claim: The company targets an average net debt to EBITDA ratio of 2.5x.
claims.quote: So, our approach to leverage, we have said that we would like to actually have a policy of average net debt to EBITDA of 2.5x.

claims.claim: The company targets 40% to 45% margin on the non-IFN and non-trucking logistics business over time.
claims.quote: So, we did say, I think in the last quarter, if I am not mistaken, we are talking about over a period of time, Logistics business to give 40% to 45% margin on the non-IFN and the non-trucking business.

risks.text: Significant management judgement required for impairment testing of goodwill and investments in subsidiaries.
Revenue recognition risks regarding completeness, accuracy, and timing of service recording in price contracts.
Related party transactions are conducted at arm's length in the ordinary course of business.
